text:
anya: heads-up — after the entropy-aware scheduler landing in canary, we’re seeing a clear eval delta on calib-enabled fp8+int4 runs. throwing this in eng-runtime for triage.
anya: summary: embeddings/structured-output tests produce more hallucinations (+3.9% on eval set) and some JSON fields get truncated when we switch kernels mid-sequence (kv cache looks ok locally but seems to drift under batching).
anya: repro steps: 1) enable entropy-scheduling 2) run nightly eval harness on mix-quant profile (fp8 kernel primary, int4 fallback) 3) observe structured-output failures in test suite 4) attach perf profile and sample outputs below.
raj: thanks — can you paste the failing example?
anya: sure, sample clipped output (expected JSON):
```
{"user": "order_123", "items": [{"id": "sku_7", "qty": 2}], "total": 39.0}
```
anya: actual (hallucinated/truncated):
```
{"user": "order_123", "items": [{"id": "sku_7", "qty": 2}], "tot
```
mike: that truncation screams KV cache misalignment when we switch kernels mid-generation. did the scheduler change the pad/offset semantics?
sophia: perf traces look like kernel stitch points at token 58 and 60 for the same request — two kernel switches inside a single response. latency is up ~18% on mix workloads compared to no-scheduler baseline.
perf-bot: nightly-eval: mix-quant-calib-run v2026-03-17: hallucination_rate +3.9%, avg_latency +17.8%, p50 token(ms) 28 -> 33, p99 token(ms) 95 -> 117
raj: interesting — the entropy scheduler tries to pick lower-cost kernels when token entropy drops, which can cause kernel switching within a response. our KV layout metadata assumes a single kernel path per request for now.
anya: right — we thought continuous-batching would handle it. But calibration uses different quant scales per kernel; when we switch, the cached KV dtype/scale may be effectively stale leading to small numeric drift and then early EOS or truncated writes.
mike: I pulled a flamegraph from the canary run:
```
- gather_kv 17%
- kernel_fp8_forward 42%
- kernel_int4_forward 30%
- kernel_switcher 3%
- serialize_out 5%
```
mike: kernel_switcher is only 3% cost but it's the pivot where state transitions happen. We probably need an explicit fence that re-normalizes KV scaling metadata on switch.
sophia: other observable: when batch size > 8 we see more switches (scheduler consolidates similar entropy samples into batches and then tries per-request kernel selection inside the batch) — so batching heuristic + entropy scheduling interplay is amplifying the issue.
raj: proposed mitigations: 1) disable intra-response kernel switching (single-kernel-per-request) as a quick canary rollback 2) add KV-scale reconciliation step on kernel switch 3) add unit test for structured-output JSON + long tokens to catch truncation.
anya: can we do 1) as hotfix and implement 2) on a follow-up? which is lower risk?
mike: 1) is easiest and low-risk — toggle in scheduler config. 2) needs kernel/runtime change and careful perf benchmarking. 3) add eval guard to block canary promotion until halluc delta < threshold.
sophia: I'll open a small PR to flip the flag in canary and run the nightly again. assigning myself.
raj: I'll draft the KV-scale reconciliation design — we need a metadata header in the KV page that contains current quant params and a cheap check that re-encodes when mismatch detected. It has to be async/cheap.
anya: action items:
- sophia: revert intra-response kernel switching in canary (ETA 1h)
- raj: design KV-scale reconciliation, bench plan (ETA EOD)
- mike: add unit/regression test for long structured outputs and token continuity (ETA tomorrow)
- anya: roll back canary if nightly delta not improved (I'll monitor)
anya: tagging @eng-ml for visibility — quant/ calibration folks, heads-up.
raj: also let's log the exact token index where switch happened in runtime traces so we can map truncation index -> switch point. will add a small trace hook.
sophia: quick note — discovered one noisy case: SPMD padding policy produced slightly different length distributions causing unexpected kernel choice. adding that to the bench matrix.
mike: ok, once revert is in I'll run the eval harness locally and post updated perf-bot numbers.
perf-bot: canary-run queued: will post results to this thread when done :hourglass_flowing_sand:
anya: thanks team — appreciate quick turnaround.
